;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Burundian unrest (2015–2018)]]
**26 people are killed in [[Cibitoke Province]], [[Burundi]]. The country's security minister attributes the attack on civilians in their houses to an unnamed "terrorist group". [http://www.latimes.com/world/africa/la-fg-burundi-attack-20180512-story.html (AP via ''The Los Angeles Times'')]
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Israel]] closes the [[Kerem Shalom border crossing]] into [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] after it is heavily damaged by a Palestinian arson attack, saying that [[humanitarian aid|humanitarian]] cases will still be allowed through while the damage is being repaired. Kerem Shalom is the border crossing where most goods transit into the [[Blockade of the Gaza Strip|blockaded territory]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/israel-closes-kerem-shalom-border-crossing-after-palestinians-break-in/4391205.html (Voice of America)]
**The [[Israeli Air Force]] destroys a [[Hamas]] tunnel more than a kilometer long that headed from [[Beit Hanun]], [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] towards [[Israel]]. [https://www.jpost.com/Arab-Israeli-Conflict/IDF-destroys-terror-tunnel-in-latest-air-strike-556222 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[2018 Paris knife attack]]
**One person is killed and four wounded in a knife attack in [[Paris]], [[France]]. The attacker is killed by police. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44096595 (BBC)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/05/12/europe/paris-stabbing-attack/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar#Shan State|Internal conflict in Myanmar § Shan State]]
**19 people are killed in clashes between the [[Myanmar Army]] and the [[Ta'ang National Liberation Army]] in [[Shan State]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/news/826/19-dead-fighting-between-myanmar-army-rebels-military-doc-14t3315 (Agence France-Presse)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Eurovision Song Contest 2018]]
**[[Israel]]i singer [[Netta Barzilai]] wins the [[Eurovision Song Contest]] in [[Lisbon]], [[Portugal]], with her song [[Toy (song)|Toy]]. This is Israel's first Eurovision win in the 21st century and fourth overall. [https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/live/2018/may/12/eurovision-song-contest-2018-live-lisbon (''The Guardian'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[EgyptAir Flight 804]]
**Relatives of the 66 people killed in the crash sue [[Apple Inc.|Apple]] alleging that an overheating [[iPad]] caused the disaster. [http://www.patentlyapple.com/patently-apple/2018/05/apple-sued-by-grieving-relatives-who-blame-the-crash-of-egyptair-flight-804-on-apple-devices-causing-a-fire.html (Patently Apple)]

;International relations
*[[Japan–North Korea relations]]
**After Japanese Prime Minister [[Shinzō Abe]] insisted North Korea settle the issue of [[North Korean abductions of Japanese citizens|Japanese citizens adbucted by North Korea]], North Korean state media [[KCNA]] accuses [[Japan]] of disrupting peace efforts before the planned [[2018 North Korea–United States summit|North Korea–U.S. summit]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2018/05/13/national/politics-diplomacy/pyongyang-blasts-japan-intervening-nuke-talks-washington/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[North Korea and weapons of mass destruction]]
**[[North Korea]] stated that it would dismantle the [[Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site]] between May 23–25 ahead of the [[2018 North Korea–United States summit|Donald Trump-Kim Jong-un]] summit meeting. Furthermore, North Korea invited journalists from the [[United States]], [[South Korea]], [[China]], [[Russia]], and the [[United Kingdom]] to cover the process. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2018/05/12/north-korea-dismantling-nuclear-test-site-may-23-25/604654002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Politics of Malaysia]]
**Former [[Malaysia]]n [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Najib Razak]] is banned from leaving the country due to the ongoing investigation into the [[1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal]]. He subsequently resigns as president of [[United Malays National Organisation|UMNO]] and as head of the [[Barisan Nasional|BN]] coalition. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-44092143 (BBC)]  [https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/424466 (''Malaysiakini'')]
**Former opposition leader [[Anwar Ibrahim]], jailed during Najib's term, is due to be released next Tuesday after receiving a [[royal pardon]]. Anwar is the leader of the [[Pakatan Harapan]] coalition that won the [[Malaysian general election, 2018|May 9 general election]]. The pardon will enable Anwar to immediately run for public office again. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/may/12/malaysia-date-set-for-release-of-opposition-leader-anwar-ibrahim (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Iraqi parliamentary election, 2018]]
**Voters in [[Iraq]] go to the polls. One quarter of the 329 seats in the [[Council of Representatives of Iraq|Council of Representatives]] must go to women. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/05/12/middleeast/iraq-elections-intl/index.html (CNN)]
**A low turnout is reported, but no bombings at polling stations. [http://www.spokesman.com/stories/2018/may/12/polls-close-across-iraq-in-first-vote-since-victor/ (AP via ''The Spokesman Review'')]
*[[Politics of Italy]]
**A court in [[Milan]] lifts the consequences of [[Silvio Berlusconi]]'s [[Trials and allegations involving Silvio Berlusconi#Tax Fraud in the Mediaset trial|2013 tax evasion sentence]]. He is now allowed to participate in elections again. [https://milano.corriere.it/notizie/politica/18_maggio_11/berlusconi-riabilitato-potra-nuovo-correre-elezioni-affa178a-555b-11e8-bf97-5f8d4271ee5b.shtml (''Corriere della Sera'')] [http://www.lastampa.it/2018/05/12/italia/berlusconi-si-pu-di-nuovo-candidare-s-del-giudice-alla-riabilitazione-3exSntp1axZPDIP0bjKr8K/pagina.html (''La Stampa'')]
*[[2017–18 Spanish constitutional crisis]]
**Writer and radical independentist [[Quim Torra]] faces his first investiture debate after being nominated yesterday for [[President of the Generalitat of Catalonia]]. In his speech, he reaffirms to continue with the [[Catalan Republic (2017)|republican]] project, to undertake a constituent process and to be under [[Carles Puigdemont]]'s directions. [https://elpais.com/ccaa/2018/05/12/catalunya/1526117680_759709.html (''El País'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/may/11/carles-puigdemont-proposes-quim-torra-successor-catalonia-government (''The Guardian'')]
**Quim Torra gets 66 votes, 2 short of the 68 votes needed to be elected by an [[Supermajority#Majority of the entire membership|absolute majority]] of the 135-seat [[Parliament of Catalonia]]. A second round is to be held on Monday, in which he would need a [[Majority#Majority vote|simple majority]] to be elected. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-spain-politics-catalonia/catalan-secessionists-fail-to-elect-new-regional-leader-idUSKCN1ID0R5 (Reuters)]
